dhpak2.8:1.1: 2.8 The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
dhpak2.8:2.1: “A monastic who delights in heedfulness,” this Dhamma {1.281} [28.325] teaching was given
dhpak2.8:2.2: by the Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to a certain bhikkhu.
dhpak2.8:3.1: It seems that this bhikkhu obtained from the Teacher a subject
dhpak2.8:3.2: of meditation leading to Arahatship and went forth to the forest.
dhpak2.8:3.3: Although he strove and struggled with might and main, he was unable to attain Arahatship.
dhpak2.8:3.4: Thereupon he said to himself: “I will ask the Teacher to explain the subject of meditation in greater detail.”
dhpak2.8:3.5: So he departed from his place of residence and set out to return to the Teacher.
dhpak2.8:4.1: On the way he saw a great forest fire raging.
dhpak2.8:4.2: Accordingly he quickly climbed up to the top of a bald mountain and sat down.
dhpak2.8:4.3: As he watched the fire consume the forest, {1.282} he concentrated his mind on the following thought:
dhpak2.8:4.4: “Even as this fire advances, consuming all fuel both great and small,
dhpak2.8:4.5: so also ought I to advance, consuming all fetters both great and small by the fire of knowledge of the noble path.”
dhpak2.8:5.1: The Teacher, even as he sat in his Perfumed Chamber,
dhpak2.8:5.2: became aware of the course of his thoughts and spoke as follows:
dhpak2.8:5.4: Just as fire consumes all fuel both great and small, so also is it necessary with the fire of knowledge
dhpak2.8:5.5: to consume and utterly destroy all fetters both small and great which arise within these living beings.”
dhpak2.8:5.6: And sending forth a radiance, appearing as though sitting face to face with that bhikkhu,
dhpak2.8:5.7: he pronounced the following verse bringing illumination:
dhpak2.8:6.1: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in
dhpak2.8:6.2: heedlessness, advances like fire burning the fetter, small or large. {1.283}
dhpak2.8:8.1: At the conclusion of the verse that bhikkhu, even as he sat there, consumed
dhpak2.8:8.2: all the fetters and attained Arahatship, together with the analytic knowledges.
dhpak2.8:8.3: And straightaway, soaring through the air, he approached the
dhpak2.8:8.4: Teacher, praising and glorifying the golden body of the Realised One.
dhpak2.8:8.5: And even as he paid homage to him, he departed.
